neighbours.label: a working part of a cutting or fastening tool in a woodworking or construction context (saw teeth, blade, screw or nail head, drill bit); the same words for body or weapon parts stay quiet
fire: A coarse handsaw has large teeth that tear quickly through rough lumber.
Before ripping the plank, he raised the circular saw blade a little higher.
Drive each screw until its head sits just below the surface of the deck.

Swap the drill bit for a larger one before boring through the stud.
The jigsaw blade snapped halfway through the plywood sheet.
Countersink the hole so the screw head will not catch on the drawer.
The chisel's edge was dull, so he honed it before cutting the mortise.
quiet: A grizzly bear has large teeth that tear quickly through raw salmon.
Before the duel, he raised the polished sword blade a little higher.
The tired child rested until his head sat just below the edge of the pillow.
The swimmer kept her head above the water as she crossed the lake.
The old horse lost a front tooth before the long winter.
The grass blade bent under the weight of the morning dew.
The mother kissed the baby's head before closing the bedroom door.
The knight's edge was his speed, so he trained before each tournament.
